title: Raised fishbone stitch
subtitle: A padded fishbone fill that lifts the leaf surface into relief
excerpt: Raised fishbone stitch adds a foundation layer of straight stitches across the leaf shape before the fishbone pairs are worked over it. The padding underneath lifts the surface stitches into a gently domed, dimensional leaf.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), fishbone stitch entry.

content.text: Raised fishbone stitch works in two stages. The first stage fills the leaf shape with straight stitches that run across the width of the shape (not along the spine). These padding stitches sit just inside the outline and give the leaf its raised, dome-like surface. The second stage works standard fishbone pairs over the padding, angling each stitch from the outer edge to meet and cross at the centre spine. The padding shows the surface stitches more clearly and adds shadow that defines the leaf.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands for padding; 2 to 3 strands for the surface fishbone

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Firm cotton or linen (a stable weave holds the padding)

content.text: Transfer the leaf outline and draw a centre spine line from tip to base. Mount the fabric in the hoop and keep it tight throughout.

Work the padding layer: bring the needle up just inside the left edge and insert just inside the right edge, making a straight stitch across the leaf. Fill the whole shape with these horizontal padding stitches, placed close together, working from tip to base.
Begin the fishbone layer at the tip. Bring the needle up at A (left edge, near the tip). Insert at B, crossing the spine by about 2 mm. This is the first left-side stitch, worked over the padding.
Bring the needle up at C (right edge, same level as A). Insert at D, crossing the spine by about 2 mm on the other side. Continue alternating left and right pairs, stepping toward the base.
Cover the padding fully so no horizontal stitches show. Secure the thread on the back. The finished leaf should have a visible domed centre spine and a smooth, filled surface.

items.symptom: The leaf feels flat, not raised
items.cause: The padding layer is too sparse or the stitches were placed outside the outline instead of inside it.
items.fix: Pack the padding stitches closely together so they form a dense cushion. They should lie just inside the transfer line.

items.symptom: The fabric puckers under the leaf
items.cause: The hoop was not tight when the padding was worked, so the weight of thread has drawn the fabric in.
items.fix: Re-mount with the fabric drum-tight before adding more padding. Use a smaller needle to reduce drag on the weave.

items.symptom: The surface stitches slide off the padding
items.cause: Surface stitches are not long enough to grip the padding layer on both sides.
items.fix: Each surface stitch should reach from the outer edge of the leaf to a clear point past the centre spine so it is held on both sides.
